National Consumer Disputes Redressal
M/S. Haryana Packaids Pvt. Ltd. Through ... vs State Bank Of India Through Its Chief ... on 30 January, 2026
NATIONAL CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION
 NEW DELHI
 JUDGMENT RESERVED ON: 31.10.2025
 JUDGMENT PRONOUNCED ON: 30.01.2026

 CONSUMER COMPLAINT NO. 28 OF 2009
 WITH
 IA/1597/2025 (Condonation of Delay)
M/S. Haryana Packaids Pvt. Ltd., Through Its Director Sh. V. S. Mann, 9, Ashoka Park
Extn, New Delhi.
 Complainant
 Versus
State Bank Of India, Through Its Chief General Manager, Local Head Office, 11,
Parliament Street, New Delhi.
 Opposite Party(s)
BEFORE:
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE A.P SAHI, PRESIDENT
HON'BLE MR. BHARATKUMAR PANDYA, MEMBER

For The Complainant : Ms. Usha Mann, Advocate
 Ms. Vijayata M. Bhalla, Advocate
 Mr. Rajiv Bahl, Advocate
 Mr. Deepak Gupta, Advocate
For The Opposite Party : Mr. Bheem Sain Jain, Advocate

 JUDGEMENT
PER HON'BLE MR. BHARATKUMAR PA ND YA, MEMBER
1. Heard Ms. Usha Mann, Advocate for the Complainant and Mr. Bheem Sain Jain,
Advocate, for Opposite Party.
2. The complaint has been filed by M/s Haryana Packaids Pvt. Ltd. (hereinafter
referred to as the Complainant), a Small Scale Industrial (SSI) unit, against the
Opposite Party - State Bank of India (SBI), alleging deficiency in service, negligence,
lack of transparency, and wrongful retention of funds. As per the complainant, the
grievance essentially arises out of the Bank's prolonged failure to provide complete and
correct statements of account, the subsequent disclosure of two undisclosed additional
accounts made under the
Right to Information Act, 2005
pursuant to directions of the
Central Information Commission, and the presence of repeated and substantial
debit/transfer entries allegedly made therein without the Complainant's mandate,
resulting in serious financial loss to the Complainant. The Complainant pleaded that it
Page 1 of 52
commenced its banking relationship with SBI, Noida Branch, in or around 1982-83, and
 maintained only two cash credit accounts with the Opposite Party, namely, Cash Credit
 (Stocks) Account No. 44906, and Cash Credit (Bills) Account No. 44907. It is
 specifically pleaded that SBI did not supply statements of account regularly and, over
 time, completely stopped providing them, thereby depriving the Complainant of access
 to its own financial records and preventing reconciliation. The Complainant alleged that
 disputes also arose when certain outstation remittances/payments received by SBI from
 customers were also not properly confirmed, accounted or intimated, and letters
 seeking clarification were not responded to. The Complainant further stated that in
 1990, it sought enhancement of credit limits to execute time-bound government and
 institutional orders, but although facilities were sanctioned, the funds were not
 effectively released in time, leading to cancellation of orders, forfeiture of earnest money
 deposits and loss of customers. A major fire incident in 1991 destroyed records and
 stocks, after which, according to the Complainant, the Bank's conduct further
 aggravated the situation and banking operations virtually came to a standstill. The
 Complainant further pleaded that the Bank initiated recovery proceedings by filing a civil
 suit in 1993, which was later transferred to the Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT). Even in
 those proceedings, SBI allegedly avoided placing complete statements of account on
 record for the earlier period. Despite repeated written requests and issuance of a legal
 notice, the Bank continued to withhold complete statements. Consequently, the
 Complainant was compelled to invoke the
RTI Act, 2005
, and filed several RTI
 applications dated 31.07.2006, 30.08.2006, 18.09.2006, 17.11.2006, 08.12.2006 and
 07.04.2007 (Annexure A). Upon SBI's continued non-compliance, the Complainant
 approached the Central Information Commission, which passed orders dated
 08.02.2007, 08.05.2007 and 10.05.2007 (Annexure C), directing disclosure. Pursuant to
 the CIC's directions, SBI supplied statements on 21.02.2007, which were illegible and
 incomplete, and thereafter on 08.05.2007, supplied legible but still incomplete
 statements for Account Nos. 44906 and 44907 (Annexure D). Significantly, for the first
 time, SBI also supplied statements of two additional accounts, namely Account No.
 44906A and Account No. 44907A, which had never been disclosed earlier and which
 were never opened or operated with its knowledge, consent or mandate and were
Page 2 of 52
L
 undisclosed and "ad hoc" accounts created by the Bank without knowledge of the
complainant. Upon examination of the statements received on 08.05.2007, the
Complainant discovered startling irregularities, including large debit entries and
withdrawals during 1989-1990 from these accounts for which no cheques were issued
by it. Several withdrawals were shown as banker's cheques/drafts allegedly issued on
the basis of "letters", which the Complainant categorically denied having issued. It was
further alleged that substantial sums were transferred to so-called "current account" and
"margin money account", whereas the Complainant asserted that it had no such
accounts at the relevant time. The disputed and allegedly unauthorised debits and
transfer entries were detailed in Annexure 'F' and quantified at approximately
?44,10,864.28 (later found to be about ?52 lakhs). The Complainant pleaded that
immediately after discovering these entries, it addressed repeated letters and
representations to SBI seeking:
i. authority/mandate for opening and operating A/c Nos. 44907A and 44907B;
 ii. details of the alleged current and margin money accounts; and
iii. vouchers and documentary basis for each disputed debit/transfer entry.
2.1 The representations relied upon include letters dated 16.05.2007, 28.05.2007,
12.06.2007, 22.06.2007, 28.06.2007, 07.07.2007, 17.07.2007, 10.10.2007 and
20.11.2007 (Annexure E). According to the Complainant, SBI avoided disclosure by
stating that records were being traced and continued to withhold the information as also
the funds. On the basis of a recast consolidated statement of all the four accounts,
excluding the illegal debits detailed in Annexure F, the Complainant pleaded that
instead of a debit balance, a credit balance of ?39,93,152.20 as on June 1992 was lying
with SBI. The Complainant claimed refund of the said amount with interest, and filed a
tentative interest calculation at 17.5% per annum with quarterly rests, totalling to
?7,03,52,671.36, as per Annexure 'G'. In addition to the above principal grievance, the
Complainant raised several connected monetary claims:
i. Payment of ?5,89,608.74 on 30.06.2006 under an RBI OTS-related context
 (Annexure H), asserted to have been made to "buy peace", with interest
 calculation Annexure I)
Page 3 of 52
ii. Wrongful retention of ?3,58,586.50 towards margin money/security in the form of
 STDRs/TDRs/DDs/POs/BGs, with interest calculation (Annexure J)
 iii. Illegal debit of ?6,314.20 on 16.04.1988, with interest calculation (Annexure K)
 iv. Retention of ? 16,250 as margin money against Bank Guarantee No. 90/65 dated
 23.07.1990, with interest calculation (Annexure L)
 v. Non-refund/non-accounting of 13 Fixed Deposit/Term Deposit/STDR receipts
 issued during 1990-91 aggregating ?2,65,675, despite instructions for renewal
 given in December 1993, with interest calculation (Annexure 'M'.
2.2 The Complainant pleaded that it being an SSI unit, was entitled to higher interest
under the
Interest on Delayed Payments to Small Scale and Ancillary Industrial
Undertakings Act, 1993
and the
MSME Development Act, 2006
, and that SBI's
continued non-disclosure and retention of funds constituted continuing deficiency in
service and continuing cause of action, causing financial loss, loss of business
reputation and mental agony. The Complainant filed this complaint on 20.02.2009 with
following prayers/reliefs before this Commission:
1. Refund Rs. 39,93,152.20 (credit balance June 1992 after removing illegal debits
 Rs.44,10,864.28) with interest Rs.7,03,52,671.36 (@17.5% quarterly w.e.f. July
 1992).
2. Refund Rs.5,89,608.74 (OTS payment 30.06.2006) with interest Rs.9,44,333.26
 (@17.5% w.e.f. 01.07.2006).
3. Refund Rs.3,58,586.50 (margin money STDR/TDR/DD/PO/BG) with interest
 Rs. 1,05,62,648.90 (@17.5% from respective dates).
4. Refund Rs. 6,314.20 (wrong interest debit 16.04.1988) with interest
 Rs.2,30,368.64 (@17.5% w.e.f. Apr 1988).
5. Refund Rs. 16,250 (BG 9065 margin 23.07.1990) with interest Rs.4,03,264.51
 (@17.5%).
6. Refund Rs.2,65,675 (13 FDs/STDRs 1990-91) with interest Rs. 15,99,822.97
 (RBI FD rates).
7. Rs. 10,00,000 compensation (mental agony/business loss).
8. Rs. 50,000 litigation costs. Grand Total (Tentative): Rs.8,51,43,109.64 (principal
 with interest) and Rs.10.50 lakhs extras
3. The Opposite Party, State Bank of India (hereinafter referred to as "the Bank"),
filed its detailed reply on 21.10.2009, along with a supporting affidavit of its authorised
officer, vehemently denying all allegations of deficiency in service, negligence, fraud,
manipulation, or unauthorised banking transactions as alleged by the Complainant. At
the outset, the Bank raised preliminary objections that the complaint is false, frivolous,
Page 4 of 52
vexatious, barred by limitation, and an abuse of the process of law, filed with the sole
intention of avoiding repayment of lawful dues and re-agitating issues already forming
subject matter, adjudicated or settled in proceedings before the Civil Court/DRT. It is
specifically pleaded that the Complainant has approached this Commission with
suppression of material facts, distorted figures, and misleading narratives, despite
having actively participated in earlier recovery proceedings initiated by the Bank in the
year 1993. The Bank pleaded that the Complainant had been maintaining regular
banking relations with SBI, Noida Branch, and was granted various cash credit and
allied facilities strictly in accordance with banking norms, duly documented through
executed loan documents, securities, and guarantees. It is stated that the
Complainant's Cash Credit (Stocks) Account No. 44906 and Cash Credit (Bills) Account
No. 44907 were operated by the Complainant itself, and all debits, credits, transfers and
charging of interest were carried out in the ordinary course of banking business, duly
authorised either through cheques, letters, or standard banking instructions and
practices. The allegation that statements of account were not supplied is denied; it is
pleaded that statements were periodically provided and that the Complainant never
raised any contemporaneous objection or representation during the relevant period of
operations (1988-1993) or thereafter till filing of the RTI Applications in 2007. The Bank
further asserted that the Complainant's financial difficulties arose due to its own
business failures, fire incident, and inability to manage working capital, and not due to
any act or omission of the Bank. With regard to the allegations concerning Account Nos.
44906A and 44907A, the Bank categorically denied that these were "secret" or
"fictitious" or unauthorised accounts. It was pleaded that these accounts were
ad-hoc/adjustment accounts opened and operated strictly in accordance with the
banking practice for operational convenience, routing of particular types of transactions,
and that the accounting entries and adjustments therein were linked to sanctioned credit
facilities. The Bank denied that any amount was siphoned off or misappropriated and
stated that all entries reflected in the statements form part of the overall banking
relationship and were duly accounted for. It was asserted that the Complainant is
attempting to misinterpret internal banking accounting mechanisms as fraudulent acts,
without any factual or legal basis. On the issue of RTI proceedings, the Bank pleaded
Page 5 of 52
that the Complainant had filed multiple RTI applications dated 31.07.2006, 30.08.2006,
18.09.2006, 17.11.2006, 08.12.2006, and 07.04.2007, and that each of these
applications was duly considered by the Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) and
replied to on legally valid grounds under the
RTI Act, 2005
. It was denied that
information was withheld arbitrarily. The Bank specifically relied upon the orders of the
Central Information Commission dated 08.02.2007 and 08.05.2007, pursuant to which
the Complainant was supplied copies of statements of account and was also granted
inspection of records on 25.05.2007 and 25.06.2007, which fact has been admitted by
the Complainant itself. The Bank denied that any illegible or incomplete information was
deliberately supplied and stated that compliance was made strictly as per CIC
directions. The Bank further pleaded that the complaint is hopelessly barred by
limitation, as the transactions complained of pertain to the period 1988-1991, whereas
the consumer complaint was filed only on 20.02.2009, after an unexplained delay of
more than 15 years. It was submitted that the cause of action, if any, had long expired
and cannot be revived by filing RTI applications or by making bald allegations of
"continuous cause of action." The Bank also raised a serious objection that the
complaint is barred by the principles of res judicata, constructive res judicata, waiver,
acquiescence, and estoppel, since the Complainant had already raised identical issues
and monetary claims by way of a belated counter-claim filed in 2001 in suit filed in 1993
by the Bank, before the Debt Recovery Tribunal, which also stood withdrawn pursuant
to a settlement. A crucial defence raised by the Bank is that during the pendency of the
DRT proceedings, the parties entered into a One Time Settlement (OTS) first in the year
2006 and again under SBI OTS-SME Scheme in 2010, which was duly accepted by the
Complainant. It was pleaded that pursuant to the compromise, the Bank withdrew its
Transfer Application (TA No. 516/2002, originally suit for recovery filed in 1993), and the
Complainant withdrew its counter-claim, which was disposed of by orders of the DRT
dated 20.07.2010. The Bank contended that once the Complainant agreed to withdraw
all claims and obtained closure of the loan account, it cannot be permitted to reagitate
or continue to agitate the monetary disputes arising from the same banking relationship
before this Commission under the purported allegations of deficient service. According
to the Bank, the present complaint is a clear attempt to renege from the compromise
Page 6 of 52
and seek unjust enrichment. The Bank specifically denied each monetary claim raised
in paragraphs 15 to 23 of the complaint, including claims for refund of alleged credit
balances, interest calculations at 17.5% with quarterly rests, refund of margin money,
STDRs, fixed deposits, and alleged wrongful debits. The Bank asserted that all interest
was charged strictly as per RBI guidelines and agreed contractual terms, that no fixed
deposit or margin money was illegally retained, and that wherever amounts were
adjusted, the same was done lawfully against outstanding dues. The Bank denied
liability under the
Interest on Delayed Payments to Small Scale and Ancillary Industrial
Undertakings Act, 1993
or the
MSME Development Act, 2006
, stating that these
enactments are wholly inapplicable to banking transactions of the present nature. The
Opposite Party Bank pleaded that the complaint does not disclose any deficiency in
service within the meaning of the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
; that the Complainant
is not a "consumer" for the purposes of the present dispute because the purpose of the
transactions of; and that the complaint is an afterthought filed with malafide intent to
harass the Bank and extract money on false grounds. Accordingly, the Bank prayed that
the complaint be dismissed with exemplary costs, as set out in the prayer clause of its
reply, and that no relief whatsoever be granted to the Complainant.
4. The complainant filed belated rejoinder on 14.08.2015 which is beyond the time
granted by the commission vide order dated 09.07.2014. Neither any application for
condoning the delay appears to be filed nor the rejoinder appears to be taken or record.
Be that as it may, the Complainant reiterated that the reply of the Bank is evasive,
misleading, and deliberately silent on crucial factual and documentary aspects. At the
outset, the Complainant specifically denied the preliminary objection that the complaint
is false, frivolous, or an abuse of process. It is pleaded that the Bank has not denied the
existence of Account Nos. 44907A and 44907B, nor has it produced any documentary
mandate, account opening forms, resolutions, or authorisation letters to establish that
these accounts were opened or operated with the knowledge or consent of the
Complainant. The rejoinder asserts that mere labelling of these accounts as "ad-hoc" or
"adjustment accounts" does not confer legality, particularly when the Bank has failed to
place on record any RBI guideline, circular, or internal policy authorising the opening
and operation of such accounts in the name of a borrower without disclosure. The
Page 7 of 52
Complainant, in its rejoinder, specifically controverted the Bank's plea that all
transactions were duly authorised and in the ordinary course of banking business. It is
asserted that despite repeated demands, including after receipt of statements on
08.05.2007, the Bank has not produced a. single cheque, voucher, letter of authority, or
mandate corresponding to the disputed debit entries and inter-account transfers. The
rejoinder emphasises that the burden to justify the debits lies squarely on the Bank, and
the Bank's failure to produce supporting documents itself establishes deficiency in
service. The Complainant further clarified that its grievance is not based on mere
accounting interpretation, but on absence of authority and non-disclosure, which goes to
the root of the banker-customer relationship. In response to the Bank's reliance on RTI
proceedings, the Complainant clarified that the rejoinder is not founded on denial of RTI
replies per se, but on the manner and timing of disclosure. It is specifically pleaded that
the existence of Account Nos. 44906A and 44907A came to light for the first time only
pursuant to CIC proceedings and inspection conducted on 25.05.2007 and 26.06.2007,
and not earlier. The rejoinder asserts that prior to 2007, the Complainant had neither
access to nor knowledge of these accounts, and therefore, had no opportunity to
question or challenge the debit and transfer entries reflected therein. Consequently, the
Bank's plea of bar of limitation is stated to be legally unsustainable, as the cause of
action arose upon discovery of concealed material facts. It is pleaded that concealment
of material facts by the Bank constitutes continuing wrong, and limitation cannot begin
to run until the customer is made aware of the wrongful acts. The rejoinder emphasises
that the Bank itself delayed disclosure of statements and underlying records for nearly
two decades, and therefore cannot take advantage of its own wrong. The Complainant
reiterated that there was no conscious waiver or acquiescence, as there was no
knowledge of the impugned accounts or transactions prior to 2007. With respect to the
Bank's reliance on the One Time Settlement (OTS) of 2010, the rejoinder categorically
denied that the settlement covered or extinguished the claims raised in the present
consumer complaint. It is pleaded that the OTS was confined strictly to the Bank's
recovery proceedings before the DRT and the counter-claim filed therein. The
Complainant clarified that at no stage did it agree to withdraw or abandon the present
consumer complaint, nor was such withdrawal a condition precedent for the settlement.
Page 8 of 52
Reliance was placed on the Complainant's letters dated 25.05.2010, 21.06.2010, and
30.06.2010, wherein it was expressly stated that withdrawal was limited to DRT/DRAT
proceedings only. The rejoinder asserts that the Bank's attempt to extend the scope of
settlement to the present complaint is contrary to record and legally impermissible. The
rejoinder further denied the Bank's contention that the Complainant is not a "consumer"
or that the dispute falls outside the jurisdiction of this Commission. It is pleaded that the
complaint squarely concerns deficiency in banking service, including non-supply of
statements, unauthorised debits, non-refund of deposits, and failure to disclose material
information, all of which fall within the ambit of the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
. The
Complainant asserted that the Bank has failed to rebut these allegations with
documentary evidence and has instead relied on bald denials and technical objections.
The Complainant reaffirmed that the reply of the Opposite Party Bank does not answer
the core issues raised in the complaint and is conspicuously silent on the absence of
mandates, vouchers, and authorisation for the disputed transactions. The rejoinder
prayed that the false and misleading defences raised by the Bank be rejected, that the
complaint be adjudicated on merits, and that the Complainant be granted appropriate
reliefs in accordance with law.
5. OP in reply filed had raised various preliminary issues on maintainibility of the
complaint. Additionally, after the settlement under OTS scheme of 2010 offered by the
OP Bank was accepted by the complainant, the OP also moved an MA on 18.05.2011
for dismissal on the ground of such settlement, which was noted in this Commission's
order dated 25.05.2011. The reply was filed by the complainant on 13.09.2011
maintaining that the present complaint and issues raised and the deficiency of service
alleged are entirely different and not part of the settlement. This Commission on
29.01.2024 passed the following detailed order to ascertain bifurcation of
settled/unsettled claims from paras 15-23 of the complaint vis-a-vis DRT Annexure-A
(Rs.1,69,81,536.12) filed along with the counter claim before the DRT. The said order
dated 29.01.2024 is reproduced herein below:
"Dated : 29 January 2024
 ORDER
 This Complaint is pending since 2009 and in the past it has also been heard on several
 occasions, nonetheless, in between certain subsequent events, had taken place after the filing of
 the Complaint that have been brought on record.
Page 9 of 52
The Complaint has been filed alleging deficiency in services on the part of the
respondent Bank in respect of clear allegations made and relief prayed for in paragraph 15 to 23
of the Complaint which is extracted hereunder:
"15. That one consolidated statement of all the above mentioned four accounts have
 been worked out by the Complainant with effect from May 1989 without the illegal
 and fictitious debit and transfer entries, bank charges, interest etc. as debited
 illegally by the officials of the Opposite Party. The Debit entries made by the
 Opposite Party in these account statements without the mandate of the Complainant
 and illegally in respect of amounts detailed in para 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 8 of Annexure 'F'
 amount to Rs.44,10,864.28p. According to this statement an amount of
 Rs.39,93,152.20p. is lying in credit with the Opposite Party bank as on June, 1992.
 Complainant is entitled to the refund of this amount with upto date interest at the
 same rate of interest as the bank had been charging in these accounts since 1989
 upto the filling of the pending suit. The Opposite Party has claimed interest @17.5%
 in its plaint in the pending case. A tentative interest calculation @ 17.5% with
 quarterly rest w.e.f. June, 1992 upto March, 2009 on the balances lying with Opposite
 Party is worked out. The tentative interest has been calculated w.e.f. July 1992 and
 the interest amount comes to Rs. 7,03,52,671.36p. This interest calculation statement
 is annexed as Annexure 'G'. The Complainant is a SSI Unit and is entitled to higher
 rate of interest under the "Interest on delayed payment to Small Scale and Ancillary
 Industrial Undertaking Act, 1993" and "The Micro, small and medium enterprises
 development Act, 2006". The Complainant reserve its right to submit a revised
 interest calculation for the period w.e.f. 1989 i.e. prior to June, 1992 and thereafter,
 on the basis of the interest which this Hon'ble Court finally decides to award to the
 Complainant in this application.
16. That the Complainant is entitled to the refund of Rs.5,89,608.74p. with upto
 date interest w.e.f. 1.7.2006. As this amount has been illegally extracted by the
 Opposite Party bank on the basis of manipulated accounts, documents and
 statement of accounts which contained fictitious entries and forged debit entries
 as explained in the above paras. This amount was deposited by the
 Complainant vide letter dated 30.6.06 with the Opposite Party Bank on the
 misconceived demand of Opposite Party Bank under the garb of RBI OTS
 Scheme for SME Sector. A copy of this letter dated 30.6.06 is annexed herewith as
 ANNEXURE 'H'. A tentative interest calculation @ 17.5.% with quarterly rest amount
 to Rs.9,44,333.26p. and the statement is annexed as ANNEXURE 'I'. Complainant is
 entitled to higher rate of interest under the abovementioned two acts i.e., the Act 32
 of 1993 and Act 27 of 2006 being a SSI Unit. This Hon'ble Commission is prayed to
 allow the Complainant the highest interest as charged by the Opposite Party in the
 accounts of the Complainant since 1989 and as reflected in the annexed statement of
 account which was provided by the Opposite Party before the CIC. Revised interest
 calculation will be submitted after the decision of this Hon'ble Commission on the rate
 of interest which is found to be entitled to the Complainant and as directed by this
 Hon'ble Commission.
17. That the Complainant is entitled to the refund of STDR, Bank drafts retained
 by the bank as margin money and as detailed in para 4 of Annexure 'F'
 amounting to Rs.3,58,586.50p. with upto date interest. Tentative interest calculation
 @ 17.5°/o with quarterly interest w.e.f. respective quarter of the fixed deposit and
 transfer of the amount to the margin money account amount to Rs.1,05,62,648.90. A
 copy of the interest calculation is annexed herewith as ANNEXURE 'J'. This Hon'ble
 Commission is prayed to allow the Complainant the highest interest as charged by
 the Opposite Party in the accounts of the Complainant since 1989 and as reflected in
 the annexed statement of account which was provided by the Opposite Party before
 the CIC. Revised interest calculation will be submitted as and when the rate of
 interest is decided by this Hon'ble Commission as entitled to the Complainant in this
 application. 18. The Complainant is also entitled to the refund of Rs.6,314.20p.
Page 10 of 52
illegally debited by the Opposite Party Bank on 16.4.1988 as described in para
 7 of the Annexure 'F' (Supra.). A tentative interest calculation @ 17.5% with
quarterly rest w.e.f. April, 1988 amount to Rs.2,30,368.64p. and the statement is
annexed herewith as ANNEXURE 'K'. This Hon'ble Commission is prayed to allow
the Complainant the highest interest as charged by the Opposite Party in the
accounts of the Complainant since 1989 and as reflected in the annexed statement of
account which was provided by the Opposite Party before the CIC. A revised
statement of interest will be submitted by the Complainant as and when this Hon'ble
 Commission decide on the rate of interest as entitled to the Complainant in this
application.
19. That the Complainant is entitled to refund of Rs. 16,250/- retained by the
 Opposite Party Bank as margin money against bank guarantee No.90/65 dated
 23.7.1990 with upto date interest as detailed in para 10 of Annexure 'F' (Supra).
A tentative interest calculation @ 17.5°/o with quarterly interest amount to
Rs.4,03,264.51p. This Hon'ble Commission is prayed to allow the Complainant the
highest interest as charged by the Opposite Party in the accounts of the Complainant
since 1989 and as reflected in the annexed statement of account which was provided
by the Opposite Party before the CIC. A revised interest calculation will be submitted
after this Hon'ble Commission decide on the rate of interest as entitled to the
 Complainant in this application.
20. That the Complainant requested the Opposite Party vide letter of December,
 1993 to continue to renew the 13 fixed deposits amounting to Rs.2,65,675/-
(which fixed deposit receipts are available with the Complainant) till the time,
same are not demanded by the Complainant. Since the Opposite Party had filed
the misconceived recovery suit in Oct., 1993 and had not been co-operating to
provide the statement of account and other details of the accounts of the
Complainant, it was apprehended that further misappropriation of the amount of
these fixed deposits may be carried out by the Opposite Party. Therefore,
Complainant requested the Opposite Party Bank to continue to renew these fixed
deposits till the same is not demanded by the Complainant. The tentative interest
calculation on the basis of the respective initial rate of interest on such fixed deposits
amount to Rs.15,99,822.97 and the statement of interest calculation is annexed
herewith as ANNEXURE 'NT. The Complainant is entitled to the interest as declared
by R.B.I. from time to time in respect of the interest rate applicable to the term
deposit/fixed deposit. The Opposite Party be directed to refund the amount of these
fixed deposits and pay the interest as per R.B.I. interest rate applicable to such time
deposit for the entire period for which the above mentioned fixed deposit remained
deposited with the Opposite Party Bank.
21. That the Complainant has suffered losses due to negligence, carelessness and
deliberate acts and omissions on the part of the officials of Opposite Party. The
Complainant has also suffered loss and injury of business and credit due to
fraudulent and forged debit entries, transfer entries, manipulation of records by the
officials of the Opposite Party and due to with holding of the material information and
the statement of account by the Opposite Party. The Opposite Party has failed to
produce the mandate of the Complainant in respect of the entries as described in
Annexure 'F' (supra). The Opposite Party Bank has also failed to provide the other
information as described in Annexure 'F' (supra). Complainant has calculated the
tentative interest on the respective amounts and has annexed the interest
calculations as Annexures herein G, I, J, K, L & M. The Complainant also reserve its
right to file revised interest calculation during the proceedings.
22. That the Complainant is a SSI Unit, is entitled to higher rate of interest under the
Act No.32 of 1993 and 27 of 2006 in the regular commercial transactions where the
due payable amounts are delayed by the purchaser. The perusal of these acts show
the intention of the legislature had all along been to protect the small scale sector and
discourage the withholding of the amounts by any party to the small scale
organizations. The SSI Sector therefore, is entitled to the higher rate of interest under
Page 11 of 52
these Acts in any eventuality of delayed payments by its parties. Keeping in line with
 this analogy, it is prayed that Complainant which is a SSI Unit and has suffered due
 to the deficiency in service and negligence of Opposite Party Bank causing extensive
 losses, therefore, higher rate of interest should be paid. Also in view of the fact that
 Complainant has suffered huge loses and had been dragged to misconceived and
 false litigations since 1993. Opposite Party has also caused losses, injury, mental
 agony and other damages to the Complainant. Therefore, the Complainant is
 entitled to compensation. An amount of Rs. 10,00,000 be awarded to the
 Complainant towards the compensation for the mental agony, harassment and
 other sufferings.
23. That the Complainant be also paid an amount of Rs.50,000/- towards the
